summary: Ammassivik Heliport (IATA: QUW) is a small helicopter facility serving the remote settlement of Ammassivik on the southern coast of Greenland. The heliport provides a vital lifeline for residents, connecting this isolated fishing community to larger towns and regional hubs. Like many heliports in Greenland, it supports both passenger transport and essential supply deliveries in a region where road infrastructure is virtually nonexistent.
faqs:
Q: What is Ammassivik Heliport used for?
A: It serves the small settlement of Ammassivik in southern Greenland, primarily providing passenger transport and connecting residents to larger communities since there are no roads in the area.

Q: Are there scheduled flights from Ammassivik Heliport?
A: Helicopter services in Greenland are typically operated by Air Greenland on a scheduled or charter basis, though frequencies to such small settlements may be limited.

Q: What facilities are available at the heliport?
A: As a small community heliport, facilities are minimal, typically consisting of a basic landing pad and possibly a small waiting shelter rather than a full terminal building.

Q: When is the heliport operational?
A: Helicopter operations in Greenland are weather-dependent and generally function year-round, though winter conditions may cause delays or cancellations.
transport_tips: Travelers typically reach Ammassivik via connecting flights from Narsarsuaq Airport or Qaqortoq Heliport, with onward helicopter legs operated by Air Greenland. Be prepared for flexible scheduling, as weather in southern Greenland frequently affects departure times. There are no roads connecting Ammassivik to other settlements, so the heliport is essentially the only way in or out for non-boat travelers.
local_tip: Pack all essentials and any specialty food items with you, as the small local store in Ammassivik has very limited supplies and the next resupply helicopter may be days away.
